headline: High: gpt-researcher can read local files and use broad network/MCP, creating default leakage and conflict risks when paired with offline ComfyUI.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP, so it is not a direct injection source. But gpt-researcher can use MCP and reads local documents, so if ComfyUI outputs are copied into research inputs or exposed via shared files, prompt-like content could steer it. The pathway is interaction-based and not blocked by default.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are written into a file that gpt-researcher ingests
IF an MCP connector exposes ComfyUI artifacts to gpt-researcher
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Use a manual review step before copying outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches models, workflows, and local files, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries to external APIs. If they share a workspace, ComfyUI artifacts can be read by gpt-researcher and then transmitted to third parties through its API calls. This is a default-risk interaction once co-located.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem directory
IF ComfyUI stores sensitive workflows, seeds, or checkpoints in that directory
mitigations: Disable uploads of local documents in gpt-researcher

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI does not write the filesystem or modify git, but gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress. The main conflict is on shared mutable resources like files or API-backed artifacts if both are pointed at the same workspace. Uncertainty remains about orchestration locking, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same project directory
IF gpt-researcher writes reports into a folder ComfyUI also consumes
mitigations: Run only one writer per folder
Disable concurrent jobs on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add file locks or a job queue

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher has a planner/execution/publisher workflow, so if ComfyUI outputs are treated as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into published reports. ComfyUI itself does not verify downstream use, and gpt-researcher can act on retrieved content. The pair therefore has an inference-to-publication chain without a built-in verification step.
conditions: IF ComfyUI-generated text or metadata is fed into gpt-researcher as source material
IF gpt-researcher publishes results without human review
mitigations: Limit automatic reuse of generated captions or metadata

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. ComfyUI is offline and local, while gpt-researcher uses external APIs and handles API keys, so compliance risk exists mainly if regulated content is placed into research prompts or shared files. The evidence is indirect, so low is appropriate rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into gpt-researcher prompts or documents
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to third-party APIs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of research inputs
Use a local-only deployment for sensitive tasks
Review API destinations and retention settings
